title: SteadyFlow batcher sleuth notes
content:
Purpose:
Quick personal scratchpad while I dig into the throughput drop on steadyflow (continuous-batching) observed in prod-dedicated last week. Trying to collect reproducible commands, logs, and lightweight hypotheses before escalating. Not a formal postmortem yet — just breadcrumbs and commands I used so others can pick up quickly.

Summary of the incident (high-level):
- Window: 2025-09-29 03:00 UTC -> 2025-09-29 09:30 UTC (customer traffic spike coincided with config change)
- Symptom: p95 token-serving latency increased from ~65ms -> ~210ms; sustained throughput drop ~28% on a small subset of pods (allocation tag: region-eu-1/sku-gpu-a10x-dedicated).
- Affected path: continuous-batching enabled routes with kv-cache warmup on (default).
- Suspected cause: misapplied continuous-batching config change (steadyflow.window.max_inflight reduced incorrectly) + interaction with kv prefill causing small batch sizes to fragment and increase per-token overhead.

Quick timeline (my notes):
- 2025-09-29 02:42 UTC: autoscaler bump (scale-up) triggered by traffic; unrelated infra noise noted in SRE channel.
- 2025-09-29 03:06 UTC: config push (rollout) for steadyflow heuristics landed: PR/#1298 (adjusted window sizing, introduced new inflight cap "steadyflow.window.max_inflight=64" for a/b test).
- 2025-09-29 03:12 UTC: first customer alert: p95 up. Alerts aggregated at 03:15.
- 2025-09-29 04:20 UTC: I snapshot controller logs and started local repro.
- 2025-09-29 09:30 UTC: reverted the change; metrics began recovering within ~12 minutes.

Commands and snippets I ran (recording exact commands to reproduce side-effects):
- Fetch pod metrics and labels (useful to identify only dedicated instances):
  kubectl -n prod get pods -l deployment=steadyflow-batcher -o wide

- Tail logs for a single pod (grep for "batch-window" and "inflight"):
  kubectl -n prod logs steadyflow-batcher-7f8c2 -c steadyflow --since=2h | egrep "batch|inflight|prefill|kvcache|latency" -n -C2 

- Quick metric pull from prometheus (p95 tokens, throughput by pod):
  curl -sG 'https://prom:9090/api/v1/query' --data-urlencode 'query=histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(token_serve_latency_bucket[5m])) by (le, pod))' | jq -r .

- Forced a local small-run load to match production shape: python3 tools/loadgen.py --target http://steadyflow-svc.prod:8080/generate --qps 180 --duration 10m --p50-ttl 30 --trace
  - Observed: average batch size collapsed from ~12 -> ~3 after the config with max_inflight=64 introduced.

- Runtime debug endpoint to inspect continuous-batcher internal state (internal admin path):
  curl -s http://steadyflow-pod:8081/_admin/continuous-batcher/state | jq
  - Key outputs I recorded:
    "window_config": {"max_inflight": 64, "max_batch_tokens": 4096, "aggressive_prefill": true}
    "prefill": {"enabled": true, "kv_hits": 0.88, "last_prefill_ts": "2025-09-29T03:10:51Z"}
    "current_inflight": 58
    "avg_batch_size_last_5m": 3.2

Error / log snippets I captured (redacted):
- 2025-09-29T03:14:22Z steadyflow-batcher-7f8c2 [WARN] batch-window: fragmented batches, expected target 12, got 3, inflight=52
- 2025-09-29T03:14:22Z steadyflow-batcher-7f8c2 [INFO] kv-prefill: candidate-key-miss=0.12, prefill-latency-ms=6.1
- 2025-09-29T03:14:22Z steadyflow-batcher-7f8c2 [ERROR] continuous-batcher: inflight-limit reached, falling back to immediate dispatch (increased per-token dispatch overhead)

Hypotheses and quick reasoning (ranked):
1) Config regression (HIGH): the new steadyflow.window.max_inflight=64 was intended to cap single-request inflight but interacts poorly with our batch formation heuristic. When inflight gets near cap, we force immediate dispatch to avoid head-of-line blocking — this reduced average batch size and increased overhead. Reverting config improved metrics. Evidence: rollback correlated with recovery; admin state showed inflight at 58 near cap.

2) Prefill/KV interaction (MED): aggressive_prefill=true + reduced window size caused many prefills to be started but not combined into batches because inflight cap forced dispatch of partially-prefilled requests. This causes both extra prefill work and smaller batches. Evidence: high kv_hits but low avg_batch_size; logs show candidate-key-miss 0.12 (so some misses causing late prefill work).

3) Autoscaler/co-scheduled interference (LOW): scale-up and node placement during the rollout might have created uneven load distribution, visible as some pods saturated while others idle. Evidence: metric aggregation shows some pods with normal p95, others high; but config change correlates more precisely with impact window.

Experiments tried and results (short):
- Local repro with original config -> avg_batch_size ~11.8, p95 token latency stable ~68ms
- Local repro with max_inflight=64 -> avg_batch_size ~3.2, p95 token latency ~220ms (matches prod directionally)
- Switch aggressive_prefill -> false locally with inflight 64 -> batch_size recovered partially (~6.1), latency improved but still worse than baseline (~110ms)
- Increase max_inflight to 128 in a canary -> batch_size returned to ~10 and latency normal; but this masks the original intent of cap (safety/backpressure).

Notes on internal heuristics (from code reading):
- batcher maintains a per-window inflight counter; when inflight >= max_inflight, the window marks any new grouping as "dispatch_immediate" to avoid queueing more work. That dispatch path does not wait to accumulate tokens beyond the currently attached request.
- KV-prefill is scheduled early but expects the regular path to coalesce similar prefills; dispatch_immediate breaks that coalescing.

Immediate mitigations (what I executed):
- Rollback PR/#1298 at 2025-09-29 09:18 UTC -> metrics started improving by ~09:30 UTC.
- Short-term config hotfix: set steadyflow.window.max_inflight=96 in region-eu-1 to relax cap (we did this for a handful of pods to restore perf while we wrote a proper fix).

Proposed longer-term fixes (rough):
- Change dispatch_immediate logic to still allow a short coalescing grace window (e.g., 2ms) when inflight is near cap; ensures partially-prefilled requests can still merge.
- Add a pref-fill/wait-aware counter: penalize prefills that start but are then immediately dispatched without coalescing to better balance prefill cost vs. latency.
- Add a canary test that runs a traffic pattern generator (we have tools/loadgen.py) exercising small bursts + warm kv cache to detect this specific regression on rollout.
- Improve rollout notes and guardrails: when changing steadyflow.window.* configs, add an automatic synthetic test run in the canary step that measures avg_batch_size and p95 against baseline.

Open questions / TODOs (for follow-up):
- Need to verify if any customers experienced token-level regressions in LLM quality (unlikely, purely perf) — loop in CS.
- Cross-check node-level telemetry during the event to see if underlying GPU utilization spiked (might hint at unrelated kernel slowdown).
- Confirm whether other regions have a different default (we saw only region-eu-1 incidence).
- Add unit test for dispatch_immediate semantics to ensure prefill coalescing when inflight near cap.

Quick reproduction scripts and notes for next person:
- To repro locally:
  1) Start steadyflow locally with config: steadyflow.window.max_inflight=64, steadyflow.window.max_batch_tokens=4096, aggressive_prefill=true
  2) Warm kv cache: python3 tools/warm_kv.py --keys 10000 --host localhost:8081
  3) Run loadgen (QPS 150-220): python3 tools/loadgen.py --target http://localhost:8080/generate --qps 180 --duration 8m --trace
  4) Inspect /_admin/continuous-batcher/state and logs for "fragmented batches"

- Useful grep patterns:
  egrep -n "fragmented batches|inflight-limit reached|dispatch_immediate|kv-prefill"

Notes to self: file this under users (scratch) then condense into a proper incident doc if needed. Marco to help with code changes for grace window. Zoe to help add canary automation.

References: JIRA INF-4821 (incident), PR/#1298 (config change), GH issue about prefills coalescing (link above).

-- end of scratchpad --
